cases.visibleGeometry: Several isolated and clustered angular high spots occupy open ground. The largest cluster lies right of centre; a curved track crosses the lower half. Context shows similar outcrops across the surrounding pasture and a pond to the west.
cases.alternatives: Exposed bedrock and loose boulders explain the irregular edges and their aerial appearance. The curved lines are visible tracks.
cases.supportLimits: Some crest cells are interpolated, so fine outlines are uncertain. The class overlay adds no coherent structure evidence.

cases.visibleGeometry: A narrow branching channel runs north to south through the patch. Rounded slopes flank it, with short parallel lines on the eastern slope and scattered small bumps. Aerial imagery shows a vegetated drainage strip; context shows it continuing far beyond the patch.
cases.alternatives: Natural erosion, a stream course and land-management terracing explain the lines and flanking slopes. Isolated bumps may be rocks or vegetation-related ground artifacts.
cases.supportLimits: The channel has substantial interpolation and a dark missing patch near its southern end. Its jagged fine structure is unreliable. No independent class pattern defines a structure.

cases.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth open ground with a broad low rise in the lower centre, a few small rocky bumps along the top edge, and a faint diagonal track. The rise lacks a crisp perimeter or level summit.
cases.alternatives: A natural undulation or bedrock swell fits the broad rise; the line is consistent with a field track and is visible in the aerial photograph.
cases.supportLimits: Ground support is predominantly measured. The relief is weak and does not form an enclosed or angular feature; sparse fine bumps offer little independent evidence.

cases.visibleGeometry: A sinuous east-west bank crosses the lower middle, separating rougher northern ground from smoother southern pasture. Small scattered bumps occur north of it; the boundary continues outside the patch. Aerial imagery places a dirt track along the bank.
cases.alternatives: A field boundary and track, with natural slope change and scattered trees or rocks, explain the visible pattern. It lacks an enclosed or discrete arrangement.
cases.supportLimits: Most ground is measured, but interpolation clusters along the bank and at trees. Its exact edge shape is less certain; the aerial track supplies a direct modern explanation.
